nodes.label: Detection Checklist (infer-conventions reference)
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Only genuine forks are listed; pure formatting and active Rector/Pint target forms are excluded because a tool already owns them.

nodes.label: Skill: infer-conventions
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Consistency first: document how the app is actually written, never propose a better pattern. Record decisions not defaults, and require at least 3 consistent examples with no meaningful rival before recording a rule.

nodes.label: Architecture Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Extract a focused business operation into an action class when it makes the operation easier to reuse or test; avoid speculative abstraction.

nodes.label: Collection Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: lazyById() is safer than lazy() when updating columns during iteration, because offset pagination can shift rows.

nodes.label: Configuration Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: env() must only be called from configuration files, because Laravel does not load .env after configuration is cached.

nodes.label: Database Performance Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: preventLazyLoading() is enabled outside production to catch N+1 issues during development rather than in production.

nodes.label: Eloquent Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Global scopes silently modify every query making debugging difficult, so they are reserved for truly universal constraints.

nodes.label: HTTP Client Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: State-changing requests are retried only when the remote API supports an idempotency key, to avoid duplicate side effects.

nodes.label: Mail Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Queued mail dispatched inside a transaction is deferred with afterCommit() so it cannot run before its data is committed.

nodes.label: Migration Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Deployed migrations are immutable because editing an old file makes fresh installations differ from upgraded installations.

nodes.label: Queue and Job Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: retry_after must exceed the longest worker timeout by a safety margin so a second worker cannot reserve a job that is still running.

nodes.label: Routing and Controller Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Controllers stay focused on HTTP concerns; an action or service is not introduced merely to satisfy an arbitrary line limit.

nodes.label: Task Scheduling Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: withoutOverlapping()'s optional value is a lock expiration in minutes, not a task timeout; too short a value permits overlap.

nodes.label: Security Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Mass-assignment protection controls which attributes may be set but does not validate values or authorize the operation.

nodes.label: Convention and Style Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Comments should explain why; clear names and small units are preferred over comments that restate an operation.

nodes.label: Validation and Forms Best Practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Validation against mutable state does not prevent a race between validation and persistence, so database constraints are still required.

nodes.label: Skill: laravel-best-practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Consistency first: the best choice is the pattern the codebase already uses, because inconsistency is worse than a suboptimal pattern.

nodes.label: Assertions
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Expected values are written or computed independently, never with the implementation's own logic, otherwise the test passes when the logic is wrong.

nodes.label: Endpoint Tests
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: 404 is returned rather than 403 for cross-tenant access because 403 confirms that another tenant's record exists.

nodes.label: Finding Test Framework Features
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: A hand-built check fails with 'false is not true' and identifies nothing, so framework assertions are preferred.

nodes.label: Fakes, Mocks, and Determinism
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Framework fakes preserve the real code path, so they are preferred over mocks, which replace the dependency.

nodes.label: Test Suite Performance
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: BCRYPT_ROUNDS=4 is set in the test environment because the default of 12 makes password hashing dominate test time.

nodes.label: Reviewing Tests
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: A passing test may still provide no value, so each test is checked for the distinct defect it would catch.

nodes.label: Security Tests
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: A defect at a security boundary is hard to detect because the feature may continue to work.

nodes.label: Factories and Test Data
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Records are created inside each test rather than in setUp() so setup stays visible and objects are not retained for the whole suite.

nodes.label: Skill: testing-best-practices
nodes.author: laravel
nodes.rationale: Project conventions take precedence over the skill; tests must verify observable behaviour and cover each changed decision.

nodes.label: .ai/rules Project Conventions
nodes.rationale: Area-grouped rules hold settled decisions, non-obvious traps and standing constraints that must be read before entering plan mode or editing files.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL via Supabase
nodes.rationale: Connection uses the pgsql driver with mandatory SSL and a private laravel schema; no credentials are stored in the repository.

nodes.label: Tailwind CSS v4
nodes.rationale: Tailwind v4 uses CSS-first configuration with the @theme directive and @import "tailwindcss" instead of @tailwind directives.

nodes.label: Laravel Boost Guidelines (AGENTS.md)
nodes.rationale: Guidelines curated by Laravel maintainers; framework and package guidance also lives in .ai/rules which must be read before planning or editing files.

nodes.label: SkillApp README
nodes.rationale: Actions, Services, Policies, Jobs, Http/Requests and Http/Resources folders are created with Artisan only when a feature actually needs them, to avoid starting with empty abstractions.

nodes.label: Policy-Level Authorization
nodes.rationale: An HTTP test cannot identify which mechanism refused the request because middleware, a policy, and abort() can all return 403, so the full permission matrix belongs in a policy or gate test.

nodes.label: Tenant Isolation
nodes.rationale: Use 404 rather than 403 for a cross-tenant request because 403 confirms that the other tenant's record exists.

nodes.label: Testing Validation
nodes.rationale: Assert the user-visible message, because a message that is present but wrong is a defect; do not assert that a rules array contains a string, because that tests the declaration and not the behavior.

nodes.label: Database Testing
nodes.rationale: Run real queries against real records; do not mock the query builder, because the test then asserts the mock. Use LazilyRefreshDatabase so a test that does not use the database skips the migrations.

nodes.label: Framework Fakes
nodes.rationale: Pass class names to fake() unless the test asserts the complete result, because a fake without class names can hide an unexpected dispatch; create fakes in the test method, not setUp(), so the dependency stays scoped to the test.

nodes.label: Outbound HTTP Testing
nodes.rationale: Call Http::preventStrayRequests() and fake the exact endpoint, because a bare Http::fake() accepts unexpected requests and can hide defects.

nodes.label: Test Naming
nodes.rationale: The name of a test method is a specification; name the behavior and result rather than the method under test, because the file name already gives the class.

nodes.label: Parallel Test Execution
nodes.rationale: A parallel run gives each process a separate database, so tests must create their own records, avoid run-order dependence, and give each process its own resource names.

nodes.label: Injection into Dynamic Query Components
nodes.rationale: Sort columns, filter fields, and sort directions are user input that affects query construction and must be tested.

nodes.label: Data Providers
nodes.rationale: Use a data provider when the setup, test body, and assertions remain the same across input values; give each case a key so a failure identifies the case without counting positions.

nodes.label: How to Find Test Framework Features
nodes.norm_label: how to find test framework features
nodes.rationale: A hand-built check fails with 'false is not true', which identifies nothing; a framework assertion names the incorrect table, value, or response so the failure indicates what to fix.

nodes.label: Fakes, Mocks, and Determinism
nodes.rationale: Tests that depend on actual time, randomness, sleeping, or network calls can fail for reasons unrelated to the code under test, so all four must be controlled.

nodes.label: Test Suite Performance
nodes.rationale: Measure before changing a setting; apply a project-wide setting only after identifying the costly work.

nodes.label: Reviewing Tests
nodes.rationale: A passing test may still provide no value, so for each test identify the defect it would catch.

nodes.label: Security Tests
nodes.rationale: A defect at a security boundary can be difficult to detect because the feature may continue to work.

nodes.label: Factories and Test Data
nodes.rationale: Creating mutable records inside each test keeps setup visible and lets each test select its factory state; setUp() objects remain in memory until the suite ends.
